tldr: On Oct 22 an arXiv paper asked when a student trained on its own sampled outputs should follow its teacher, a refinement of on-policy distillation (OPD). By Oct 30 papers had applied OPD to multi-agent routing and to rerankers, and on Nov 8 one measured how much quantized or asynchronous rollout mismatch OPD tolerates.
whats_new: Nov 9: Agentic-OPD, an arXiv paper, argues that keeping only the best-validation checkpoint from GRPO agent training discards capabilities, and uses on-policy distillation to recover them.
why_it_matters: On-policy distillation is moving from a training trick into agent post-training and serving components, and its rollout cost now has a studied trade-off against quantized or asynchronous inference.
take_for_builders: If you RL-train agents with GRPO, keep intermediate checkpoints instead of only the best-validation one until Agentic-OPD's recovery results are reproduced; none of these papers has independent replication yet.

beats.headline: Advantage-based method decides when the student should follow the teacher
OPD moves into multi-agent routing and decision-model rerankers
beats.summary: EvoRouter targets multi-agent serving configuration cost; DecisionRank distills LLM ranking into a model that scores without decoding.

beats.headline: Study tests how much training-inference mismatch OPD tolerates
Agentic-OPD recovers agent skills lost to best-checkpoint selection

open_questions: Does the advantage-based method beat plain on-policy distillation on agentic tasks, not only its own benchmarks?
Do EvoRouter's cost savings hold on production query mixes outside its own benchmark?
Does DecisionRank's distilled reranker match its LLM teacher's ranking quality on a third party's data?
What quantization level or rollout staleness does the mismatch study find safe for OPD students?
Does any group release code that reproduces Agentic-OPD's capability recovery on a different agent benchmark?
